text:
•
Air conditioning condensing units  (casement/ window unit/ split type) must not cause any vibration in the building
•
Rubber padding should be provided at the base of the air-conditioner condensing unit (ACU)
•
No hacking of holes or openings through existing reinforced concrete structures within the unit
•
Air conditioner pipe must not be embedded in reinforced concrete slabs, columns or beams
•
For pre-cast facade with tiles, a single opening of 50mm x 50mm per panel for the running of refrigerant pipe is allowed. However, you should ensure that your air conditioning condensing unit installer checks the wall tiles surrounding the opening for bolts and refrigerant pipes. Any delaminated tiles will have to be removed
•
The air conditioning condensing unit installer has to ensure that precautions are taken during the installation for public safety
•
If you wish to have an air conditioning condensing unit installed in your living room where an existing gas pipe passes through, you must engage a licensed gas service technician to check that the gas pipes and/ or installation comply with the Code of Practice (CP) 51, clause 7.2.7, ‘pipes in enclosed or unventilated areas’ before proceeding with the installation
Maintenance
•
You must maintain the external wall face free from stains at all times at your own expense
•
Perform regular maintenance in your air-conditioner to avoid causing any inconvenience or nuisance to your neighbours
•

Town Council’s conditions
The Town Council has imposed the following conditions for flats which have an air-conditioner installed on their air conditioning condensing unit ledge.
•
Do not tamper with the air conditioning condensing unit ledge
•
Ensure that air conditioning condensing unit ledge is kept clean and free of obstruction at all times
•
Grant HDB, Town Council, other Government authorities and their authorised persons access into your flat to facilitate necessary checks on the air conditioning condensing unit ledge if the need arises

Preparing your HS during a wartime emergency
The HS is only to be occupied during a wartime emergency. During a wartime emergency, the SCDF will inform residents to prepare their HS for occupation. To find out how to prepare your HS for occupation, please refer to SCDF Emergency Handbook (Chapter 4 on Wartime Emergencies - Shelter Protection) for more information. You can download a copy of the SCDF Emergency Handbook via
https://www.scdf.gov.sg/home/community-volunteers/publications
.

text:
The goal is to recreate the soft, even glow of natural daylight, making a space feel brighter, airier, and less enclosed.

Best installation practices:
DO: Install in enclosed spaces (bathrooms, corridors, walk-in wardrobes)
DO: Integrate into recessed/false ceiling
DO: Use evenly diffused daylight-mimicking lighting
DO: Keep surrounding ceiling design clean and understated
DO: Treat as architectural lighting feature
DON'T: Install in rooms with ample natural light
DON'T: Mount directly onto flat ceiling
DON'T: Use harsh, uneven lighting creating hotspots
DON'T: Oversize or make it the focal point
DON'T: Expect identical appearance to real skylight

Effective locations: Bathrooms, hallways, kitchens, walk-in wardrobes.

text:
Yes, faux skylights can be installed in HDB flats.

Critical ceiling height requirements:
• Recommended: 2.6m structural ceiling minimum
• False ceiling reduces height by 150–200mm
• Resulting finished height: approximately 2.4–2.45m
• Marginal ceiling (2.4m): not recommended for recessed installation (results in 2.2–2.25m finished height)

Alternative for low ceilings: surface-mounted faux skylights that sit directly against existing ceiling.

Most BTO flats built from 2018 onward have 2.6m structural ceilings; older resale flats vary considerably.
